utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Madam Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-98- 29-A, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. May I call for appearances, please. The appellant.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. On behalf of General Galic, Mara Pilipovic, lead counsel, and Stephane Piletta-Zanin, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Steffen Wirth appearing for the Prosecution and with Miss Helen Brady, and our case manager today is Miss Victoria McCreath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Today's proceedings, a Status Conference, which is actually the fourth, the last one having been held on the 11th of March this year. And the purpose of our status conference, as usual, under Rule 65 bis, is that for persons who are in detention pending appeal, such as the appellant is, awaiting his appeal, he should be afforded an opportunity to appear before the Court to express any concerns he may have regarding his appeal or detention conditions and also to be updated with respect to the status of the case. So having said that, I will ask the appellant first, Mr. Galic, whether he has anything he wishes to state and whether there are any concerns regarding his conditions of detention. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. First of all, let me take this opportunity to thank the Tribunal and the Court for the fact that they allowed me to leave because of my sister. I do have a number of questions, but I would especially like to thank the Trial Chamber for this decision. Secondly, there's nothing much to say about my health except that on the 16th of May I visited a neurologist, and he said to me that in as far as my spinal cord injury in the course of my rest was concerned, that neither surgery nor any medication can help me. All I can do is accept the fact that I'll have to suffer. I must say that I found it rather difficult to cope for a while afterwards. However, two days ago I was referred for treatment, special spinal treatment, and I have to say that it does seem to me that it is rather promising. So I'm hopeful, especially because after that bleak prognosis that I was given back in May, this represents a ray of hope. This is all the latest news since the last Status Conference, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. On behalf of the Appeals Chamber, I wish to express grateful thanks to the authorities at the Detention Unit for affording the appellant all these opportunities and possibilities to look after his health, and I'm glad to know that the latest treatment is promising, and hopefully that will lead to better health for the appellant. I now wish to look at the status of the case. So far, of the four motions that the Appeal Chamber has had on additional evidence, the decisions have already been granted for the first and third Rule 115 motion. And for the fourth Rule 115 motion, the Appeals Chamber is still considering it. It may be issued in due course. The second one was already dealt with. There is also the Prosecution's request for leave to file a consolidated further response to Defence replies concerning the third and fourth Rule 115 motions, which are still pending. I would like to find out from the parties whether there is anything they wish to raise. I will begin with the appellant's counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, possibly, Madam President. The Defence had the opportunity to discuss a certain number of issues with General Galic this morning in order to try and prepare for the defence of the accused as well as possible. And so this morning we've developed a certain number of points, especially with regard to chronology. Could the Trial Chamber let us know whether -- I mean, if at all possible - - approximately at what point in time you believe that this case will be dealt with by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I take it you mean when the appeal will be set for hearing by the Appeals Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. That's what I've just said, Madam Chair. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is not possible to give a date right now because this appeal is actually on the queue together with other appeals which were filed before the Galic appeal before the Appeals Chamber. So the Appeals Chamber tries as much as possible to follow the sequence of the appeals before it. And also, as you know, the same Appeals Chamber has appeals from the International Tribunal for Rwanda, so it's quite a long list on the case list for the Appeals Chamber. So as much as possible, the Appeals Chamber does try to list for hearing appeals as quickly as they can, but the workload is such that it's not possible at the moment to be able to say when the Appeals Chamber thinks the hearing can be set for this particular appeal. Otherwise, that would be kept into momentum on the cause list before the Appeals Chamber. I would like to find out whether the respondents, the Prosecutor's party has anything to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WIRTH
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have nothing to raise. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And in addition to what I've just said about the workload, looking at the progress of the case or the procedural history, quite a lot has been happening in this case. And as soon as the final motion for additional evidence is dealt with, steps will be taken, I'm sure, for the Appeals Chamber to set dates for the hearing of this particular appeal. Any other matter from the appellant's side?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just want to address the appellant that as his lawyers have said, that they've been discussing the preparation of the final solutions for this appeal and are anxious to find out the date. I just want to assure Mr. Galic that everything is being done. As soon as the other appeals have come off the list, this particular appeal will be scheduled for hearing. If not towards the end of this year but at least early next year. There being no other matters to deal with, I'll adjourn the hearing until the next Status Conference. The Court will rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
